title: Beyond the 956: North Carolina woman arrested at home after flashing headlights to warn drivers about police
excerpt: Hailey Brown of Lowell, North Carolina, says a Gaston County police officer followed her home and pulled her out of her house after she flashed her headlights to warn other drivers about a police car parked in the median. She now faces four charges, which she disputes.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Hailey Brown of Lowell, North Carolina, says she was arrested at her own front door after flashing her headlights to warn other drivers about a police car parked in the median — and she now faces four charges.

Brown told WCNC Charlotte she was driving home from work shortly after 2 a.m. on Thursday, November 19, along Wilkinson Boulevard near Westover Street, when she spotted a Gaston County police vehicle parked in the median with its lights off. She flashed her headlights to alert approaching drivers, something she said she routinely does when she sees police, crashes, or other hazards on the road.

Brown said she had already pulled into her driveway when the officer turned around and activated his emergency lights. She said she did not realize the officer was trying to pull her over, and she did not want to talk to him at her home in the middle of the night.

As she tried to close her front door, Brown said the officer forced it open and pulled her outside. “He, like, flew like a linebacker. I was going to shut my door, and he busted my door open, and he started ripping me out of my house,” Brown told WCNC. Doorbell camera video shows officers taking Brown to the ground outside her Lowell home as her grandmother, who lives with her, pleaded with them to get off her. Brown said she was left with bruising on her arm.

Brown spent several hours in jail and was released early Thursday morning, according to WCNC. She is due back in court in January.

According to the arrest report cited by WCNC, Brown allegedly resisted, delayed or obstructed an officer by running from her vehicle during a traffic stop after being ordered to stop. Brown disputes that account, saying she never realized a stop had been initiated. She is also charged with displaying an expired registration, operating a vehicle without a current inspection, and failing to dim her headlights.

North Carolina has no law specifically prohibiting motorists from flashing their headlights to warn other drivers about police presence. An attorney who spoke to WCNC said flashing headlights to communicate the presence of police is generally considered protected expression under the First Amendment.

The Gaston County Police Department is reviewing the officers’ use of force, Assistant Police Chief Anderson Holder confirmed to WCNC. Brown is demanding the release of body-camera and dashboard-camera footage.

All charges are allegations. Brown is presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.
